reason: I'll strengthen the bones first; the picture shows spaces for mineral and says it resists compression.
expectation: I expect the mineral to make the living bone framework harder or better able to resist compression.

alternatives.reason: I could build the front muscle first, but I want to strengthen the framework before adding muscles.

effect: The mineral strengthened the bones while leaving the joint movable. Next I'll build a muscle.
reaction: It was useful to see that the living cells and soft joint tissues remain.
reason: The front attachments show where muscle cells can go; I'll start there before building the opposite side.
expectation: I expect a muscle to form between the front tendons, though I'm not sure exactly how it will be assembled.

alternatives.reason: The back muscle is also needed, but either side seems reasonable to start with.

effect: The front cells formed the biceps, whose pull bends the elbow. I’ll build the muscle on the other side next.
reaction: The arrows made the connection between the muscle’s position and bending clear.
reason: The back attachments are the remaining place to build a muscle, and this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a muscle to form behind the elbow and pull the forearm in the opposite direction.

effect: The triceps result confirmed that the same kind of muscle cells can straighten the elbow when attached behind it. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The comparison with the biceps made the importance of attachment position clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the biceps and triceps was most worthwhile because the arrows showed how muscles on opposite sides bend and straighten the elbow.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the second muscle was a little repetitive as an action, even though the comparison was useful; it was the only combination offered.

surprise.text: The same kind of muscle cells could produce opposite movements because of where they attach.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary: the pictures and goals explained where the mineral and muscle cells belonged.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because seeing how the same pulling cells make opposite movements made me curious about other body structures.
